query: Which method can be used for concurrent strength–ductility improvement, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The concurrent strength-ductility improvement in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can be achieved through the formation of a single-phase microstructure with a body-centered cubic (BCC) or face-centered cubic (FCC) crystal structure, which can be obtained by controlling the composition and processing conditions of the alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy (HEA) with a multi-component system
generation.intervention: Control of composition and processing conditions
generation.conditions: Equilibrium or non-equilibrium processing conditions, such as powder metallurgy, mechanical alloying, or laser powder bed fusion
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a single-phase microstructure with a BCC or FCC crystal structure
generation.mechanism: The single-phase microstructure leads to improved strength and ductility due to the reduction of grain boundary segregation, lattice distortion, and the formation of precipitates or secondary phases
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength and ductility of the HEA
generation.baseline: Conventional HEAs with inferior castability, segregation, and strength-ductility conflict
generation.boundary: The composition and processing conditions of the alloy, such as the selection of principal elements, powder morphology, and consolidation methods
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanisms of the formation of the single-phase microstructure and its effect on the strength and ductility of the HEA are not fully understood and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of composition and processing conditions to investigate the effect on the microstructure and mechanical properties of the HEA
measurements: Microstructure characterization using SEM, TEM, and XRD
Mechanical testing, including tensile and compressive testing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the formation of a single-phase microstructure with a BCC or FCC crystal structure does not lead to improved strength and ductility, the hypothesis is falsified
